svg.font-family: Inter, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: MAX22200: Application diagram
svg.desc: Schematic of the MAX22200 application diagram: the chip with U2 MCU, C1 capacitor 0.1 µF, C2 capacitor 0.1 µF, C3 polarized-capacitor 10 µF, C4 capacitor 2.2 µF, C5 capacitor 22 nF, C6 capacitor 1 µF, R1 resistor 15 kΩ, R2 resistor 10 kΩ, R3 resistor 10 kΩ, L0 solenoid, L1 solenoid, L3 solenoid, J1 DC motor, J2 Latched valve; the MCU wires carry the port hooks GpioRead(CtrlPin::Fault), GpioSet(CtrlPin::Cmd), GpioSet(CtrlPin::Enable), Transfer().
svg.text: The data sheet's application diagram on a 24 V supply: L0 on OUT0 driven high side to GND, L1 on OUT1 low side from the supply, the latched (bistable) valve between OUT2 and OUT3 as a full bridge, L3 on
OUT4 and OUT5 in parallel, low side, and a brushed DC motor between OUT6 and OUT7. The MCU drives SPI, CMD and ENABLE, reads FAULT, and may pulse TRIGA; TRIGB is grounded, so channels 4 to 7
switch over SPI. Above each MCU wire: the port hook that drives it. Datasheet: Typical Application Circuits; Application Diagram, p. 44.

* Not confirmed in the datasheet: R1 15 kΩ: an example inside the 15 kΩ to 100 kΩ range; 15 kΩ gives IFS = 1 A; R2 10 kΩ: the application diagram shows the FAULT pull-up without a value; R3 10 kΩ: the application diagram shows the SDO pull-up
without a value; net +3V3: the data sheet does not say where the pull-ups go; the MCU's logic supply is assumed.
